description: A step rail for a multi-step form — numbered markers joined by connectors, over the headless Tabs. Each marker is a real tab: activation, `aria-selected`, the roving tabindex, Home/End and `disabled` all come from Tabs, restyled as a circle. `orientation` picks the rail direction; sized xs–xl, and `data-density` scales each size further.

props.name: activationMode
props.description: When a focused trigger becomes active; see {@link TabsActivationMode}.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Value of the tab active on first render.

props.name: dir
props.description:
Reading direction; see {@link TabsReadingDirection}. Inherited from the
nearest `DirectionProvider` when omitted, falling back to `"ltr"`.

props.name: lazyMount
props.description:
When `true`, a panel's children are not rendered until that tab is first
activated. Once mounted they remain in the DOM across subsequent tab
switches (lazy mount, not unmount-on-hide). Useful for panels that own
expensive initialisation — e.g. a scroll-snap carousel whose initial
scroll position must be set while the panel is visible.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fired on every user-driven activation with the activated tab's metadata.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the requested value when the user activates a tab.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the currently active tab.

contractProps.name: size
contractProps.description: Rail size; `data-density` scales each size further.

dataAttributes.name: data-state
dataAttributes.when: any step that is not current (set by Tabs)

dataAttributes.name: data-step-state
dataAttributes.when: the step is not yet done — the default

dataAttributes.name: data-step-state
dataAttributes.when: the step is done — the marker becomes a tick

dataAttributes.name: data-step-state
dataAttributes.when: the step failed validation — the marker becomes a warning glyph, kept even while a later step is current

dataAttributes.name: data-orientation
dataAttributes.when: the rail runs horizontally — the default (set by Tabs)

dataAttributes.name: data-orientation
dataAttributes.when: the rail runs vertically (set by Tabs)

props.name: ariaLabelledBy
props.description:
Id of an existing element to use as the tablist's accessible name,
set as `aria-labelledby`. Mutually exclusive with `label`.

props.name: label
props.description:
Accessible name for the tablist, announced as `aria-label`. Pick a
short, human-readable description of the set (e.g. `"Account
sections"`, not `"Tabs"`). Mutually exclusive with `ariaLabelledBy`.

contractProps.name: compact
contractProps.description: Collapses the rail into a progress bar — the same steps, drawn as segments with their markers and labels hidden. For narrow containers, where a labelled rail cannot fit. The steps stay in the DOM, so each panel keeps the `aria-labelledby` pointing at its trigger; swapping the rail out for a hand-rolled bar would break that. Drive it from the consumer side (e.g. `useMediaQuery`), and pair it with your own "Step N of M" line — Stepper owns no step data model.

props.name: value
props.description:
Identifies this trigger, linking it to the `Tabs.Content` of the same
value. Not the visible label — use `children` for that.

props.name: asChild
props.description:
Render the child element instead of the default `<button>`. All tab
ARIA attributes and event handlers are merged onto the child. The child
must accept a `ref`. Useful for routing links that need tab semantics.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
Removes the trigger from the roving tab order and marks it
`aria-disabled`/`data-disabled`; arrow-key navigation skips it.

props.name: ref
props.description:
Ref to the rendered element. Defaults to `HTMLButtonElement`; when using
`asChild`, specify the child's element type (e.g. `HTMLAnchorElement`).

props.name: state
props.description:
The progress this step carries in its own right, published as
`data-step-state`. Deliberately independent of which step is *current* —
that is `data-state="active"`, owned by {@link Stepper}'s value — so a
failed step keeps its error marker while the user stands on a later one.

{@link StepperMarker} reads this to decide whether to render its children
(the step number), a tick, or a warning glyph.
- `upcoming` — Not yet done (the default).
- `complete` — Done; the marker becomes a tick.
- `error` — Failed validation; the marker becomes a warning glyph.

props.name: value
props.description: Value of the trigger this panel belongs to.

elements.example: Your account details. Where should we send the receipt? Check everything before you submit.

api.description:
`<primitiv-stepper>` — a step rail for a multi-step form. The behaviour is a WAI-ARIA tab set's, exactly as React's registry Stepper composes Tabs: each step's `<button>` becomes a tab, so activation, `aria-selected`, the roving `tabindex`, Home / End and `disabled` are all Tabs'. What the stepper adds is its own names, `manual` activation by default (browsing the steps never changes step, so nothing half-typed in a panel is lost), and each step's progress written onto its button as `data-step-state`.

For a server-validated form, cancel `primitiv-stepper-change`, post the step, and let the response move the user on: set `value` to the next step, and `state="complete"` or `state="error"` on the one just submitted.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The current step's value. Reflected: it moves as the user changes step, so a server re-render or a history snapshot sees the live step.

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.description: Which way the rail runs, which picks the arrow-key pair. Defaults to `horizontal`.

attributes.name: activation-mode
attributes.description: `manual` waits for Enter or Space; `automatic` changes step as focus arrives. Defaults to `manual`.

events.name: primitiv-stepper-change
events.description: Bubbles, cancelable, fired before a user-driven change of step is applied. Call `preventDefault()` to keep the user on the current step.

api.description: `<primitiv-stepper-list>` — the rail, a tablist. Structural: the root writes its ARIA.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: The rail's accessible name. Give this or `aria-labelledby`.

api.description: `<primitiv-stepper-step>` — one step. It decorates exactly one child you write (a `<button>`), which becomes the tab and carries the step's marker, label and description.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The step's value, pairing it with the panel of the same value.

attributes.name: state
attributes.description: The progress the step carries in its own right, written on its button as `data-step-state`. Independent of which step is current, so an errored step keeps its error while the user stands on a later one. Defaults to `upcoming`.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: A step the user cannot reach yet: arrow keys still land on it, but it never activates.

api.description: `<primitiv-stepper-panel>` — a step's body, a tab panel. Structural: the root writes its ARIA.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: The panel's value, pairing it with the step of the same value.

events.name: primitiv-stepper-show
events.description: Bubbles from the panel as its step becomes current (not on first render), so a lazy panel can fetch its content.
